homozygous FGF3 mutations lead to a new type of syndromic congenital deafness characterized by the complete absence of inner ears (Michel aplastic ear) and that these mutations cause this syndrome by interfering with the induction and/or early differentiation of the inner ear.
homozygous FGF3 mutations result in a new autosomal recessive malformation syndrome characterized by inner ear aplasia, microtia and microdontia.

the identification of the genetic cause of syndromic microtia and deafness, and the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms of FGF3 gene action in the pathogenesis of this syndrome.
